findings.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:30 uses String#scrub which requires Ruby 2.1, but the repo targets Ruby 2.0, causing NoMethodError on every PollFeed execution

poll_feed.rb:30 calls i.content.scrub without a nil guard; many RSS feeds expose content as content_encoded or only description, so i.content is nil and a single content-less item aborts the entire polling run mid-way

embed_controller.rb:15 uses params.require, a Rails 4 strong-parameters API, but the repo's default Rails 3 bundle has no require method, so every request to embed/best fails with NoMethodError instead of the intended 404

New gems ruby-readability, guess_html_encoding, and simple-rss are added only to Gemfile_rails4.lock and not to the parallel Rails 3 lockfile, causing dependency resolution failures and LoadError on the Rails 3 bundle

New top-level assets embed.js and embed.css are never registered in config.assets.precompile, so rake assets:precompile in production omits them and the embed feature 404s on the deployment path it targets

Migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb is edited in place to add force: true; the edit is a no-op for databases that already ran it, and re-execution would silently drop and recreate top_topics, discarding computed topic stats

No HTML sanitization in the PollFeed import pipeline: unescaped feed HTML passes directly to TopicEmbed.import with raw_html cook method, bypassing the sanitization pipeline, and is rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` — allows script injection/XSS in feed content (Confidence 75, P1)

poll_feed.rb: `i.content` is assumed to exist on every feed item; RSS/Atom items with only `<description>` have nil content and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire hourly poll mid-run with retry: false so the failure is silent (Confidence 75, P2)

embed/loading.html.erb: no failure/terminal state for the embed — if retrieval silently fails (invalid host, recently retrieved, unresolvable username, Sidekiq fetch failure), the loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no signal to the consumer (Confidence 75, P2)

poll_feed.rb: `feed_key` (Last-Modified/conditional-GET tracking) is defined but never called — dead code from an unfinished conditional-poll optimization, causing full feed fetch and re-parse every hour (Confidence 100, P3)

lib/topic_retriever.rb: retrieval throttle uses non-atomic separate SETNX and EXPIRE commands — if the process dies between them, the key exists without TTL and that embed URL is throttled forever with no recovery path; should be SET key val NX EX 60 (Confidence 50, P2)

Only Gemfile_rails4.lock was updated for the new ruby-readability and simple-rss gems; the primary Gemfile.lock is stale, breaking non-Rails4 builds, especially under --frozen deployment pinning (Confidence 50, P2)

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb: no tests exercise the actual feed-parsing path — all tests stub poll_feed itself, so real RSS/Atom XML is never run through SimpleRSS.parse → TopicEmbed.import, leaving the 'RSS and Atom feeds both import correctly' criterion unverified (Confidence 75, P2)

embed.js: no guard for a missing `#discourse-comments` element — `comments.appendChild(iframe)` throws TypeError on mis-installed pages, silently killing embedding with only a console error (Confidence 50, P3)

No sanitization on the imported-HTML path: Post#cook short-circuits for raw_html cook_method, TopicEmbed.import stores feed content verbatim with skip_validations, and best.html.erb renders it with raw, so untrusted feed HTML (including PollFeed content that bypasses readability's whitelist) can inject scripts into the embedding site

TopicEmbed.import unescapes/unescaped interpolation of a remote URL into stored HTML: the 'imported_from' link builds an anchor from url with only a /^https?/ check, allowing injection of markup like '><script> via crafted embed URLs
Disqus importer regression: removal of --category option and original timestamps (created_at: Date.parse) means imported threads lose their real creation dates and category placement

PollFeed job crashes on feeds without a content field: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError for RSS 2.0 description-only or Atom summary-only feeds, and with retry: false one bad item aborts the entire poll so later items are never imported

Dead code in PollFeed: feed_key is defined but never used, so the intended 'only re-import when the feed changed' logic was never implemented, causing hourly re-parsing and full PostRevisor revisions of changed items

TopicRetriever.perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire scheduled PollFeed job inline during embed URL retrieval, doubling feed-poll load, adding full feed latency to the retrieval path, and failing the user's retrieval if the feed errors

Untraceable edits to already-shipped migrations: adding force: true to create_table :top_topics is destructive (drops/recreates the table on re-run, discarding ranking data), and migrate_word_counts gets whitespace-only churn
Dangling admin menu entry: client.en.yml adds an 'Embedding' admin menu string but the diff contains no corresponding admin view, route, or controller

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29-34: No error isolation around the per-item import loop; i.content can be nil for Atom feeds (which use description/summary), causing NoMethodError that aborts the entire rss.items.each iteration
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb: With sidekiq_options retry: false, a single malformed feed entry permanently kills feed importing with zero error surfacing until the article ages out of the feed

lib/topic_retriever.rb:29-34: retrieved_recently? uses non-atomic $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire; if the process dies between them the key persists with no TTL and retrieval is permanently blocked until the key is manually deleted; should use SET key val EX 60 NX (or MULTI)
lib/topic_retriever.rb: The 60s throttle is set before retrieval succeeds, so a failed fetch (network error, 404) still consumes the throttle window for all users

app/models/topic_embed.rb:24,78: embed_url is stored and matched raw with no normalization (scheme, trailing slash, query/UTM params, case); URL variants like http vs https or with utm_source params create duplicate topics for the same article since exact string equality/unique index don't catch them

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:5-6 + app/models/topic_embed.rb:28-32: topic_id/post_id are null: false but have no foreign key and no dependent cleanup, allowing dangling topic_embeds rows when an imported post/topic is hard-destroyed; schema should enforce this with FK ON DELETE CASCADE
app/models/topic_embed.rb:28-32: When embed.post is nil from a dangling row, PostRevisor.new(nil) raises and, due to missing error isolation, the entire hourly poll dies at that item every hour

app/models/topic_embed.rb:32-33: content_sha1 is updated unconditionally and outside a transaction even when revisor.revise! returns false or partially fails, so the hash drifts from actual post content and the 'update only if changed' guard enforces a weaker invariant than intended

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14 + app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-10: Loading view reloads every 30s with no terminal state and each reload re-enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) for embeds that will never appear, generating a Sidekiq job per visitor every 30 seconds indefinitely with no cap, backoff, or dead-end message

app/models/topic_embed.rb:49-52 + app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:27: Outbound fetches via open(url).read have no open timeout (open-uri default open_timeout is nil) and no size cap, so a wedged remote site can hang a Sidekiq job indefinitely and a large response is fully materialized in memory
lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117,143-145: Unversioned breaking change removes the --category/-c option from the disqus import contract, breaking existing scripted invocations with 'Unknown option' errors

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143-145: The new import path makes one dead link (open(t[:link]) raising) abort the entire import loop with no rescue, dropping every thread after the failing one and leaving already-created topics half-populated with replies silently skipped

config/site_settings.yml:353-357: Architecture hardwires 'exactly one embeddable host and one polled feed' into global settings while the topic_embeds table is per-URL/per-host; supporting a second site forces schema/settings migration, and all three enforcement points (EmbedController, TopicRetriever, PollFeed) must change in lockstep

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117-149: The --category/-c option is deleted and import logic replaced with TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently breaking existing automation invoking 'thor disqus:import -c' with unrecognized-option errors and changing output from local permalink posts to network fetches dependent on remote site availability

db/migrate/20131223171005:4: Adding force: true to the pre-existing create_table :top_topics migration will drop and recreate the table on re-run (rollback/re-migrate), destroying accumulated top-topic statistics

db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb: Whitespace-only churn (trailing space and EOF newline changes) to an already-shipped migration, indicating unreviewed mutations outside the stated scope

app/models/post.rb:131-135: Validation is inverted — the cooking pipeline (including sanitization) is bypassed for embed-imported posts (raw_html cook method returns raw unfiltered), and embed/best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked, so third-party HTML from poll_feed.rb and TopicEmbed.import (with skip_validations: true) can inject script tags, event handlers, or javascript: hrefs, causing persistent XSS

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:30 uses String#scrub which requires Ruby 2.1, but the repo targets Ruby 2.0, causing NoMethodError on every PollFeed execution

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `i.content.scrub` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, and `String#scrub` is not available on older Rubies. However, the proposed finding’s key claim—“the repo targets Ruby 2.0”—is not established anywhere in the provided diff (no Ruby version pin, CI config, or similar evidence). Without verifiable context that the project must run on Ruby < 2.1, concluding this will cause `NoMethodError` is speculative rather than a definite defect in the change itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:30 calls i.content.scrub without a nil guard; many RSS feeds expose content as content_encoded or only description, so i.content is nil and a single content-less item aborts the entire polling run mid-way

embed_controller.rb:15 uses params.require, a Rails 4 strong-parameters API, but the repo's default Rails 3 bundle has no require method, so every request to embed/best fails with NoMethodError instead of the intended 404

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbedController#best` using `params.require(:embed_url)`, which is valid in Rails 4 (strong parameters) and also available in Rails 3 when the `strong_parameters` gem is used. Nothing in the diff shows the app is running under a Rails 3 stack without strong-parameters; in fact, the only lockfile touched is `Gemfile_rails4.lock`, suggesting this code path targets the Rails 4 bundle. Therefore the claim that every request will fail with `NoMethodError` due to missing `require` is not verifiable from this diff and is likely a mis-assumption about the runtime Rails version/gems.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New gems ruby-readability, guess_html_encoding, and simple-rss are added only to Gemfile_rails4.lock and not to the parallel Rails 3 lockfile, causing dependency resolution failures and LoadError on the Rails 3 bundle

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to the main `Gemfile` (so they are not “only” added to `Gemfile_rails4.lock`). While `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated to reflect these new dependencies (including `guess_html_encoding` as a transitive dependency), the diff does not show any “parallel Rails 3 lockfile” at all, nor any bundling process that would fail because it wasn’t updated. Therefore the claim about causing Rails 3 dependency resolution failures/LoadError is not directly verifiable from this diff and is partly based on a misreading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New top-level assets embed.js and embed.css are never registered in config.assets.precompile, so rake assets:precompile in production omits them and the embed feature 404s on the deployment path it targets

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new standalone assets `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` and `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and references the stylesheet via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` in the new embed layout. However, the claim that these assets will be omitted in production because they are “never registered in config.assets.precompile” cannot be verified from this diff: no `config/initializers/assets.rb` (or equivalent Discourse asset pipeline configuration) is shown, and Discourse may already precompile additional/non-application assets via an existing wildcard or custom precompile list. Therefore the 404 outcome is plausible under default Rails settings, but not provably introduced by this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb is edited in place to add force: true; the edit is a no-op for databases that already ran it, and re-execution would silently drop and recreate top_topics, discarding computed topic stats

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` would drop and recreate the table *if the migration were executed against a DB where `top_topics` already exists*, Rails migrations are versioned and normally run only once; databases that already ran this migration will not re-run it, and fresh databases won’t have the table yet so `force: true` has no effect. The finding’s data-loss scenario depends on atypical/manual re-execution or a mismatched schema state, which is not a verifiable problem introduced by this diff in the normal migration flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No HTML sanitization in the PollFeed import pipeline: unescaped feed HTML passes directly to TopicEmbed.import with raw_html cook method, bypassing the sanitization pipeline, and is rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` — allows script injection/XSS in feed content (Confidence 75, P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an import path where feed-provided HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, it takes `i.content` from the parsed feed, does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Finally, the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This combination means malicious feed HTML (e.g., `<script>` or event handlers) can be persisted and executed in the embed iframe/page, i.e., an XSS vector.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil it enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic and renders `embed/loading`. adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb: `feed_key` (Last-Modified/conditional-GET tracking) is defined but never called — dead code from an unfinished conditional-poll optimization, causing full feed fetch and re-parse every hour (Confidence 100, P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined (intended to memoize a Redis key based on the feed URL) but it is never referenced anywhere in the job (`execute` only calls `poll_feed`, and `poll_feed` directly does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of `feed_key`). That makes `feed_key` dead/unused code in this diff. The finding’s additional explanation about Last-Modified/conditional GET is somewhat speculative (no conditional request logic exists here), but the core issue—unused method suggesting incomplete optimization—is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb: retrieval throttle uses non-atomic separate SETNX and EXPIRE commands — if the process dies between them, the key exists without TTL and that embed URL is throttled forever with no recovery path; should be SET key val NX EX 60 (Confidence 50, P2)

adjudication.rationale:
In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle is implemented as:

- if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
    $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
    return false
  end

This uses two separate Redis commands (SETNX then EXPIRE). If the process crashes or is interrupted after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the key will remain without a TTL. In that state, subsequent calls will see setnx return false and will treat it as "retrieved recently" forever (until manual key deletion), which is a real correctness bug in the throttling logic. Using an atomic command (e.g., SET key val NX EX 60) would avoid this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Only Gemfile_rails4.lock was updated for the new ruby-readability and simple-rss gems; the primary Gemfile.lock is stale, breaking non-Rails4 builds, especially under --frozen deployment pinning (Confidence 50, P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Gemfile` updated and `Gemfile_rails4.lock` updated to include `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss`, but it does not show whether a primary `Gemfile.lock` exists at all, nor does it show it being out of date. Concluding that “non-Rails4 builds” will break due to a stale `Gemfile.lock` is not directly verifiable from this diff alone; it depends on repository files and build/deploy workflow not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb: no tests exercise the actual feed-parsing path — all tests stub poll_feed itself, so real RSS/Atom XML is never run through SimpleRSS.parse → TopicEmbed.import, leaving the 'RSS and Atom feeds both import correctly' criterion unverified (Confidence 75, P2)

adjudication.rationale: In the added spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, every example only checks that execute either does/doesn’t call poll_feed based on settings, and never invokes poll_feed itself. The actual implementation in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb (SimpleRSS.parse(open(...)) then rss.items.each { TopicEmbed.import(...) }) is therefore untested: no fixture RSS/Atom XML is parsed, no open-uri interaction is exercised, and no assertions are made about items being converted into TopicEmbed.import calls. So the claim that the feed-parsing/import path (including RSS vs Atom variations) is unverified by tests is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js: no guard for a missing `#discourse-comments` element — `comments.appendChild(iframe)` throws TypeError on mis-installed pages, silently killing embedding with only a console error (Confidence 50, P3)

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `comments` is assigned via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then used unconditionally as `comments.appendChild(iframe)`. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and calling `appendChild` will throw a TypeError at runtime, preventing the rest of the embed logic from running.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No sanitization on the imported-HTML path: Post#cook short-circuits for raw_html cook_method, TopicEmbed.import stores feed content verbatim with skip_validations, and best.html.erb renders it with raw, so untrusted feed HTML (including PollFeed content that bypasses readability's whitelist) can inject scripts into the embedding site

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`, using the provided `contents` (from feeds) essentially verbatim aside from URL absolutization and appending a footer. The feed polling path (`Jobs::PollFeed`) passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` straight into `TopicEmbed.import` without any whitelist filtering (unlike `import_remote` which uses ruby-readability with tag/attribute lists). Finally, the embed view renders `post.cooked` with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Together, this makes it possible for untrusted feed HTML (e.g., `<script>`/event handlers) to be stored and rendered as executable HTML in the embed iframe (and anywhere else that renders `cooked` as HTML), constituting a real XSS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import unescapes/unescaped interpolation of a remote URL into stored HTML: the 'imported_from' link builds an anchor from url with only a /^https?/ check, allowing injection of markup like '><script> via crafted embed URLs

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends HTML containing an `` tag built via string interpolation: `"#{url}"`, with only a `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` check. That regex only enforces the prefix and does not prevent quotes or angle brackets in the remainder of `url` (e.g., `http://example.com/'>

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus importer regression: removal of --category option and original timestamps (created_at: Date.parse) means imported threads lose their real creation dates and category placement

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the importer previously accepted a --category option, looked up category_id, and created the topic via PostCreator with both created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) and category: category_id. The diff removes the --category option and all category_id handling, and replaces the PostCreator call with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]). TopicEmbed.import_remote / TopicEmbed.import do not pass created_at or category into PostCreator, so imported Disqus threads will no longer preserve the original thread timestamps and cannot be placed into a specified category via CLI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed job crashes on feeds without a content field: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError for RSS 2.0 description-only or Atom summary-only feeds, and with retry: false one bad item aborts the entire poll so later items are never imported

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. With `simple-rss`, item fields like `content` are not guaranteed to exist for all feeds/items (many RSS 2.0 feeds use `description` only; Atom may have `summary`), so `i.content` can be `nil`, and calling `.scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire job mid-loop. Since the job doesn’t rescue per-item, one malformed/missing-content item prevents later items from being imported; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` there will be no automatic retry of the job run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code in PollFeed: feed_key is defined but never used, so the intended 'only re-import when the feed changed' logic was never implemented, causing hourly re-parsing and full PostRevisor revisions of changed items

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` is defined (building a Redis-style key based on the polling URL) but it is never referenced anywhere in the diff. As implemented, `poll_feed` always fetches and parses the feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterates over all items every time the scheduled job runs (hourly), with no conditional using `feed_key` (or other caching) to skip work when the feed hasn’t changed. The claim about an intended “only re-import when feed changed” mechanism is inferred from the unused `feed_key` name, but the dead/unused code and the unconditional hourly re-parse are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever.perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire scheduled PollFeed job inline during embed URL retrieval, doubling feed-poll load, adding full feed latency to the retrieval path, and failing the user's retrieval if the feed errors

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (not enqueued), which calls `poll_feed` and performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without any rescue. This means every embed retrieval attempt (after throttle and only when the embed isn’t already present) can synchronously fetch and parse the full feed, adding feed latency to the retrieval path and increasing feed polling beyond the scheduled hourly job. If `open`/parse raises (network/feed error), the exception will bubble and abort the retrieval job, preventing the embed from being created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Untraceable edits to already-shipped migrations: adding force: true to create_table :top_topics is destructive (drops/recreates the table on re-run, discarding ranking data), and migrate_word_counts gets whitespace-only churn

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can destroy existing `top_topics` data if the migration is re-run (e.g., rollback/redo or in a partially-migrated environment). The `migrate_word_counts` change shown is whitespace-only churn and not itself a functional problem, but the `force: true` change in an already-existing migration is a real, verifiable risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dangling admin menu entry: client.en.yml adds an 'Embedding' admin menu string but the diff contains no corresponding admin view, route, or controller

adjudication.rationale: The added `embedding: "Embedding"` string in `config/locales/client.en.yml` aligns with the new `embedding:` section added to `config/site_settings.yml` (with settings like `embeddable_host`, `feed_polling_enabled`, etc.). In Discourse, admin “settings categories” are typically rendered by the generic site-settings UI based on `site_settings.yml` groups and localized labels, not by adding a dedicated route/controller/view per category. So this is not a verifiable dangling menu entry from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29-34: No error isolation around the per-item import loop; i.content can be nil for Atom feeds (which use description/summary), causing NoMethodError that aborts the entire rss.items.each iteration

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is nil (which can happen depending on feed format/fields; many feeds provide `description`/`summary` instead), calling `.scrub` on nil will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire `rss.items.each` processing for the job since there is no per-item rescue/handling. This is a concrete failure mode introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb: With sidekiq_options retry: false, a single malformed feed entry permanently kills feed importing with zero error surfacing until the article ages out of the feed

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and does not rescue per-item errors, so an exception (e.g., from `open(...)`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, or `i.content.scrub` when `i.content` is nil) would abort that run and Sidekiq would not retry it. However, this is a `Jobs::Scheduled` job with `recurrence { hourly }`, so a failure does not “permanently kill feed importing”; it will be attempted again on the next scheduled run. Also, exceptions are still surfaced in Sidekiq logs/monitoring even if retries are disabled. Thus the finding overstates the impact in a way that isn’t verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:29-34: retrieved_recently? uses non-atomic $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire; if the process dies between them the key persists with no TTL and retrieval is permanently blocked until the key is manually deleted; should use SET key val EX 60 NX (or MULTI)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb retrieved_recently? sets a throttle key using `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then, in a separate call, `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic. If the process crashes or loses connectivity after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE is applied, the key will remain without a TTL, causing `setnx` to keep failing and `retrieved_recently?` to return true indefinitely, permanently throttling retrieval for that embed_url until the key is manually deleted. Using `SET key val NX EX 60` (or a MULTI/transaction/Lua script) would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb: The 60s throttle is set before retrieval succeeds, so a failed fetch (network error, 404) still consumes the throttle window for all users

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `retrieve` calls `retrieved_recently?` before `perform_retrieve`. In `retrieved_recently?`, the Redis key (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`) is set via `setnx` and given a 60s expiry immediately when it is not present, and only then does `retrieve` proceed to `perform_retrieve`. Since `perform_retrieve` (and especially `fetch_http` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `open(url)`) can fail/raise due to network errors/404/etc. with no rescue here, a failed retrieval attempt will still leave the throttle key set for 60 seconds, preventing further attempts during that window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24,78: embed_url is stored and matched raw with no normalization (scheme, trailing slash, query/UTM params, case); URL variants like http vs https or with utm_source params create duplicate topics for the same article since exact string equality/unique index don't catch them

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the lookup `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` rely on exact string equality, and `topic_id_for_embed` similarly plucks by exact `embed_url`. The diff shows no normalization/canonicalization of URLs (scheme changes, trailing slashes, case, query params like UTM). Therefore semantically equivalent URL variants will be treated as distinct and can create duplicate topics/embeds for the same article despite the unique index.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:5-6 + app/models/topic_embed.rb:28-32: topic_id/post_id are null: false but have no foreign key and no dependent cleanup, allowing dangling topic_embeds rows when an imported post/topic is hard-destroyed; schema should enforce this with FK ON DELETE CASCADE

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new `topic_embeds` table with `topic_id`/`post_id` declared `null: false` and the `TopicEmbed` model only has `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` with no foreign-key constraints in the migration. However, the finding’s claim about “no dependent cleanup” and “dangling rows when an imported post/topic is hard-destroyed” is not directly verifiable from the diff: there are no changes showing posts/topics are hard-deleted, nor any association additions on `Topic`/`Post` that would or wouldn’t handle dependent deletion. Lack of DB-level FKs/ON DELETE CASCADE is a design/integrity preference, not a concrete defect demonstrated by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:28-32: When embed.post is nil from a dangling row, PostRevisor.new(nil) raises and, due to missing error isolation, the entire hourly poll dies at that item every hour

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing TopicEmbed row is found, the code does `post = embed.post` and then (if the content hash changed) calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)`. There is no guarantee in this diff that `topic_embeds.post_id` always points to a still-existing Post: the migration adds `post_id` with `null: false` but no foreign key/cascade, so deletions can leave a dangling row. If `embed.post` is nil, `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will raise and PollFeed (which iterates items without rescue and is scheduled hourly with `retry: false`) will abort on that item each run. This is a real robustness/correctness issue in the introduced code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32-33: content_sha1 is updated unconditionally and outside a transaction even when revisor.revise! returns false or partially fails, so the hash drifts from actual post content and the 'update only if changed' guard enforces a weaker invariant than intended

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing embed is found and content_sha1 differs, the code calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then always executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking the return value of `revise!` or wrapping both operations in a transaction. Since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return false (e.g., `should_revise?` is false when the computed new raw equals the current raw), the SHA can be advanced even when the post content is not updated. Also, because the SHA is computed from `contents` before `absolutize_urls`, the guard can trigger even if the resulting stored raw would be unchanged, increasing the chance of drift.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14 + app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-10: Loading view reloads every 30s with no terminal state and each reload re-enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) for embeds that will never appear, generating a Sidekiq job per visitor every 30 seconds indefinitely with no cap, backoff, or dead-end message

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view contains JS that `document.location.reload()` every 30s. So as long as the embed never gets created (e.g., retrieval fails, invalid/mismatched `embed_url`, missing `embed_by_username`, etc.), the client will keep re-requesting `/embed/best`, and each request will enqueue another `:retrieve_topic` job. There is no controller-side dedupe/backoff/terminal error message. While `TopicRetriever` has a 60s Redis throttle that may make many jobs exit quickly, it does not prevent the repeated job enqueuing described in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:49-52 + app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:27: Outbound fetches via open(url).read have no open timeout (open-uri default open_timeout is nil) and no size cap, so a wedged remote site can hang a Sidekiq job indefinitely and a large response is fully materialized in memory

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two outbound HTTP fetches using Ruby's open-uri without any timeout or response size limiting: (1) app/models/topic_embed.rb `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` fully reads the entire remote response into memory and does not pass `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`; (2) app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` also performs a remote fetch without timeouts. With open-uri defaults, timeouts are not explicitly set here and the calls can block a Sidekiq job for an unbounded time on slow/hung servers, and `.read` can materialize arbitrarily large responses in memory. This is directly verifiable from the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117,143-145: Unversioned breaking change removes the --category/-c option from the disqus import contract, breaking existing scripted invocations with 'Unknown option' errors

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Thor CLI option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and also deletes the associated logic that reads `options[:category]` and passes `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. After this change, any existing invocation like `thor disqus:import --category ...` (or `-c`) will be rejected by Thor with an unknown option error, so it is a verifiable breaking change in the task’s interface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143-145: The new import path makes one dead link (open(t[:link]) raising) abort the entire import loop with no rescue, dropping every thread after the failing one and leaving already-created topics half-populated with replies silently skipped

adjudication.rationale: Yes that risk is introduced by the diff: `Disqus#import` now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` inside the threads loop, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no rescue. If `open(t[:link])` raises (dead link/timeout/HTTP error), the exception will bubble up and terminate the Thor task, so remaining threads won’t be processed. However, the claim about “already-created topics half-populated with replies silently skipped” is overstated: the failure happens before any topic/post creation for that thread (since `open(url).read` occurs first), and an exception would not be silent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/site_settings.yml:353-357: Architecture hardwires 'exactly one embeddable host and one polled feed' into global settings while the topic_embeds table is per-URL/per-host; supporting a second site forces schema/settings migration, and all three enforcement points (EmbedController, TopicRetriever, PollFeed) must change in lockstep

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce global site settings (`embeddable_host`, `feed_polling_url`, `embed_by_username`) and the new logic in `EmbedController`, `TopicRetriever`, and `Jobs::PollFeed` consistently uses those single values. However, this is an intentional product/architecture choice reflected in the setting descriptions (singular “Host”, singular “URL”, singular “username”), not a verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness defect. The `topic_embeds` table being per-URL does not inherently require multi-host/multi-feed support; `embed_url` already encodes the host and a single configured host is coherent. The claim about needing schema/settings migrations and changing components “in lockstep” is a speculative maintainability concern contingent on an unstated requirement (supporting multiple sites/feeds), not a concrete problem demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117-149: The --category/-c option is deleted and import logic replaced with TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently breaking existing automation invoking 'thor disqus:import -c' with unrecognized-option errors and changing output from local permalink posts to network fetches dependent on remote site availability

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes all logic that used `options[:category]` to look up a category_id and pass it to `PostCreator`. With this change, any existing automation calling `thor disqus:import -c ...` will now pass an unknown option and Thor will raise an unrecognized/unknown option error. The import behavior also changes from creating a simple local post containing a permalink to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which performs `open(url).read` and Readability parsing, making the import dependent on remote site availability and content at runtime. These are concrete, verifiable behavior/API changes introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005:4: Adding force: true to the pre-existing create_table :top_topics migration will drop and recreate the table on re-run (rollback/re-migrate), destroying accumulated top-topic statistics

db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb: Whitespace-only churn (trailing space and EOF newline changes) to an already-shipped migration, indicating unreviewed mutations outside the stated scope

adjudication.rationale: The diff in db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb only removes a trailing-space line and changes the file’s final newline (shown by the `\ No newline at end of file` marker). There is no functional change to the migration logic. Calling this a “real problem” (bug/security/correctness defect) isn’t verifiable from the diff; it’s at most unnecessary whitespace churn / process commentary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131-135: Validation is inverted — the cooking pipeline (including sanitization) is bypassed for embed-imported posts (raw_html cook method returns raw unfiltered), and embed/best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked, so third-party HTML from poll_feed.rb and TopicEmbed.import (with skip_validations: true) can inject script tags, event handlers, or javascript: hrefs, causing persistent XSS

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff explicitly adds a `:raw_html` cook method in `Post#cook` that returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where sanitization would typically occur). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, using `contents` taken from RSS (`poll_feed.rb` uses `i.content`/`i.id`/`i.link` with no HTML sanitization) or remote readability content. The embed UI then renders `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`; for `raw_html` posts, `post.cooked == post.raw` per the new logic/tests. This combination makes it possible for third-party feed/article HTML to be stored and rendered as-is (including `<script>`, event handlers, or `javascript:` URLs), i.e., a persistent XSS vector introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:19: The origin check uses substring matching (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)), so an origin like 'http://eviltrout.com.evil.net' passes a discourseUrl of 'http://eviltrout.com', allowing a hostile framing page to spoof discourse-resize messages and inject arbitrary iframe heights (layout-spoofing/clickjacking surface)
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using indexOf/substring matching for origin validation is insecure and can be bypassed with a malicious lookalike domain (e.g., subdomain or prefixed domain) that contains the trusted domain string, allowing an attacker to pass the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31-34: The code assumes every feed item has a 'content' field; the first item without a <content> element (common in Atom feeds with only <summary>) raises NoMethodError, killing the hourly poll and all embedding for that site despite the advertised RSS/ATOM support

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the poll loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is nil for a feed item (e.g., when the parser only exposes `summary`/`description` and not `content`), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError` and abort the job. There is no nil-check or fallback, so the job can be killed by a feed item lacking `content` despite the comment claiming RSS/ATOM support.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb: String#scrub requires Ruby >= 2.1 but the codebase still targets Ruby 1.9 per the Gemfile comment

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` the new code calls `i.content.scrub` (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`). `String#scrub` is not available on older Rubies (it was added in Ruby 2.1), so running this job on Ruby 1.9/2.0 would raise `NoMethodError`. The Gemfile nearby still references Ruby 1.9 support (“perftools only works on 1.9 atm”), so this is a real compatibility/correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85: Changing @post.save to @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) makes every caller of revise! honor a skip-validations flag, allowing embed updates to skip length/spam validations that apply to ordinary edits — a silent widening of the accepted constraint that all post edits are validated

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change behavior in `PostRevisor#update_post` from always validating (`@post.save`) to optionally skipping validations when `opts[:skip_validations]` is passed (`@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`). However, in this diff the only shown new use is `TopicEmbed.import` calling `revise!` with `skip_validations: true` specifically for imported/embed content, and the codebase already uses `skip_validations` in `PostCreator` for the same embed-import path. There’s no evidence in the diff that user-controlled callers can now bypass validations unintentionally, so this reads as an intentional feature to support imports rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: `cook_method: raw_html` in app/models/post.rb:131-134 combined with app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 bypasses the entire sanitization pipeline on attacker-influenced RSS feed content, allowing persistent script execution via unsanitized content rendered with `raw` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:20

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. The diff introduces a path where remote/untrusted HTML can be stored and later rendered without sanitization:
- `Post#cook` now returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`app/models/post.rb`).
- `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). `absolutize_urls` only rewrites leading-slash href/src; it does not sanitize tags/attributes or block `javascript:` URLs, inline event handlers, etc.
- Feed polling (`Jobs::PollFeed`) uses `i.content` from the RSS/Atom feed directly (only `CGI.unescapeHTML` / `scrub`), then calls `TopicEmbed.import`, so attacker-controlled feed content can include `<script>` or dangerous attributes and will be persisted.
- The embed rendering uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), which will output the stored HTML unescaped; with `raw_html` cooking, `cooked` effectively becomes the unsanitized `raw`.
This is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff (at least for the embed iframe view, and potentially anywhere else that renders `cooked`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reflected/stored XSS via unescaped URL interpolation into HTML in app/models/topic_embed.rb:12 — user-supplied `embed_url` is interpolated into an HTML attribute/string with no escaping, allowing injected markup like `<svg onload=...>` to be stored in post body

Reflected XSS in app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:10 — `request.referer` (client-controlled) interpolated raw into inline `<script>` JavaScript string context; `ensure_embeddable` host check does not prevent breaking out of the JS string literal
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying vulnerability: the client-controlled `request.referer` header is interpolated into inline JavaScript without proper escaping, enabling XSS (breaking out of a JS string literal).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SSRF in app/models/topic_embed.rb:42 and app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — server-side fetch of attacker-influenced URL via open-uri follows redirects unrestricted with no re-validation, allowing redirection to internal hosts (e.g., 169.254.169.254) with content exfiltrated through the public embed page
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe an SSRF risk in the PollFeed scheduled job due to calling open/open-uri on an attacker-influenced SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without adequate validation, enabling fetching arbitrary internal/external URLs (candidate also notes redirect-based bypass and mentions an additional file, but the core issue matches).

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage origin check in app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:16 uses substring match (`indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of equality, allowing origins containing the forum origin as a substring (e.g., example.com.evil.com) to pass the check

adjudication.rationale: In embed.js the check is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) return;`, i.e. it accepts the message only when the configured `discourseUrl` string contains the message’s `e.origin`. The proposed bypass (`example.com.evil.com` passing because it contains the forum origin as a substring) would require the opposite comparison (checking whether `e.origin` contains `discourseUrl`). With the code as written, a longer origin like `https://example.com.evil.com` will not be a substring of `https://example.com/...` and will be rejected. So the specific security issue claimed is not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:34-37 — 'delegates to poll_feed' test mocks the method under test, leaving the entire real poll_feed implementation (link/id fallback, user.blank? branch, CGI.unescapeHTML on nil content) with zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the “delegates to poll_feed” example stubs SiteSetting values and sets `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once`, so it verifies `execute`’s conditional delegation without running `poll_feed`. That does mean `poll_feed`’s internal behavior isn’t exercised by this spec, but that’s a test-coverage gap rather than a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the diff. The spec is correctly testing `execute`, not incorrectly mocking the method it is directly testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError on Atom entries where content is nil

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. This will raise `NoMethodError` if `i.content` is `nil` because `nil.scrub` is invalid. RSS/Atom items parsed by `SimpleRSS` may not always have a `content` field (some feeds provide `description`, `summary`, etc.), so this is a real runtime defect introduced by the diff due to missing nil-handling (e.g., `i.content.to_s.scrub`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:30-42 — 'valid host' tests stub both retrieved_recently? and perform_retrieve, so the real throttle (redis setnx/expire), no_throttle staff bypass, and perform_retrieve body are never exercised

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “with a valid host” examples do stub retrieved_recently? (and only assert whether perform_retrieve is called), so they do not exercise the real Redis throttle logic in retrieved_recently? nor the body of perform_retrieve. However, that is a test-coverage critique rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect in the production code introduced by this diff; the spec is explicitly unit-testing control flow of #retrieve and it’s not inherently wrong for it to stub collaborators.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:38-41 — 'Supports updating the post' test never verifies the content_sha1 state transition (update via update_column) nor that re-import with unchanged content does not create a revision

adjudication.rationale: The cited example test (“Supports updating the post”) only asserts that a second `TopicEmbed.import` call results in `post.cooked` containing “new contents”. It indeed does not assert that `embed.content_sha1` changes via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)`, nor does it test the no-op case where re-importing identical content avoids a revision. However, this is a test coverage critique, not a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the diff—the functionality may still be correct even without those assertions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:46-51 — 'creates a topic view' test renders against a bare mocha mock, making response.should be_success a tautology that never validates the actual best.html.erb template rendering

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` the "creates a topic view" example only asserts that `TopicView.new` is invoked; it does not render/validate `best.html.erb` output (RSpec controller specs don’t render views unless `render_views` is enabled). However, the proposed finding’s rationale (“renders against a bare mocha mock”) is off: no mock `@topic_view` is provided, and the spec is simply not exercising template rendering at all. This is a test coverage/style critique rather than a verifiable bug/correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:37-41 — TopicRetriever.expects(:new) has no with(...) constraint, so arguments passed by the controller (embed_url, no_throttle flag) are unverified

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no topic is found it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`; it does **not** call `TopicRetriever.new` directly or pass any `no_throttle` flag. The proposed finding claims the controller passes `(embed_url, no_throttle)` into `TopicRetriever.new` and that the spec fails to verify those args, but that’s a misread of the diff. While the spec does use `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` without a `with(...)` constraint, this is at most a test-specificity nit and is not tied to real arguments being passed by the controller as stated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration creates topic_embeds with no foreign keys on topic_id/post_id and no dependent: :destroy cleanup, so deleting a topic/post leaves orphaned rows that wedge the PollFeed job — PostRevisor revises a deleted post or raises NoMethodError on nil, aborting the loop mid-way so later feed items never import, and retry: false swallows the failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces TopicEmbed rows that reference topics/posts only via integer columns (no DB foreign keys in the migration) and TopicEmbed.import assumes the associated post always exists. In the update path, it does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` when content changes; if the post was deleted but the topic_embeds row remains, `embed.post` will be nil and PostRevisor will raise (likely NoMethodError), aborting PollFeed’s `rss.items.each` loop. PollFeed is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so such a failure would not be retried. While the absence of `dependent: :destroy` cannot be fully verified from this diff alone (it would live on Topic/Post associations elsewhere), the nil-post/orphan handling issue is a real defect in the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Orphaned topic_embeds rows permanently block re-importing the same embed_url due to the unique index on embed_url

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. `TopicEmbed.import` looks up an existing row by `embed_url` and, if found, it does not create a new topic/post/embed; it assumes `embed.post` exists and uses it for updates. The model does not specify any `dependent: :destroy` behavior, and there are no foreign keys shown, so if the associated `post`/`topic` is deleted elsewhere, the `topic_embeds` row can remain orphaned. In that case, future imports of the same URL will always hit the existing `TopicEmbed` row and will not be able to recreate the topic/post, effectively blocking re-importing (and may even error when `embed.post` is nil). This failure mode is implied directly by the unique index + lookup logic + lack of cleanup handling in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false rewrites the entire posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PostgreSQL, blocking all reads and writes with no disable_ddl_transaction!/multi-step strategy

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` that does `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` with no `disable_ddl_transaction!` and no multi-step/backfill approach. On PostgreSQL (especially versions prior to the “fast default” optimization), adding a column with a non-NULL default can trigger a full table rewrite and requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock during the operation, which blocks reads/writes on `posts`—a high-risk change for a large table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to an already-shipped migration (create_table :top_topics) means a rollback-and-rerun will silently DROP and recreate the populated top_topics table, destroying computed topic stats with no backup step

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In normal Rails migration workflows, this migration will not be re-run on already-migrated databases, so the new `force: true` has no effect there. If someone does a rollback/redo, the rollback of a `create_table` in a reversible `change` already drops the table, so data loss would occur regardless of `force: true`. `force: true` mainly affects the case where the migration is run while the table already exists (it will drop/recreate instead of raising), which is not the “rollback-and-rerun” scenario described. Therefore the finding is a misreading and not a clearly verifiable new defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :top_topics ... force: true in a shipped migration changes its meaning for databases that already ran it, causing silent data loss on re-run
force: true on create_topic_embeds silently drops existing embed mapping rows in partial/rerun scenarios with no export

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` creates the table with `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table first if it already exists, then recreate it. If this migration is run in an environment where `topic_embeds` already exists (e.g., partial/failed deploy, manual table creation, schema drift, or migration rollback/re-run), all existing rows (embed mappings) would be silently destroyed. This data-loss behavior is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: t.string :embed_url capped at 255 chars with a unique index causes TopicEmbed.create! to raise for longer article URLs inside the Topic.transaction, aborting the whole PollFeed run with retry: false, and since the transaction rolls back nothing is persisted so the job fails identically every hour with no repair path

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateTopicEmbeds`, `t.string :embed_url` uses Rails’ default `string` length (typically VARCHAR(255)). `TopicEmbed.import` then does `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a `Topic.transaction` without rescuing errors. If an RSS item URL exceeds the column limit (a realistic possibility), the insert can raise (e.g., PG “value too long”), rolling back the transaction and bubbling the exception up to `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, which also doesn’t rescue—so the entire poll run aborts. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, that failed execution won’t be retried immediately; it will likely fail again on the next scheduled run if the same long URL remains in the feed.
